newsitem.title: UK: Dresdner Kleinwort Benson chairman resigns.
newsitem.headline: Dresdner Kleinwort Benson chairman resigns.

text.p: London-based investment bank Kleinwort Benson, owned by Germany's giant Dresdner Bank AG, said on Friday its chairman Simon Robertson had resigned and would be replaced by current non-executive chairman Lord Walker.

In a statement issued simultaneously in Britain and Germany the chairman of the Dresdner group Juergen Sarrazin said Robertson's departure followed differences of opinion about how best to integrate the bank's resources in London and Frankfurt.
While Walker will be the non-executive chairman, the investment bank's executive committee will now be chaired by Hansgeorg Hofmann, deputy chairman of Kleinwort Benson group.

"All of us are agreed that, to recognise the full potential of Dresdner Kleinwort Benson, we must now fully integrate our resources in London and Frankfurt, so that they and all our offices operate as one entity," the Dresdner chairman said.
"Sadly, we have differed with Simon about the way this is best achieved," Sarrazin added.

"We deeply deeply regret the departure of Simon. He has made a very significant contribution to Kleinwort Benson and the successful creation of Dresdner Kleinwort Benson, our global investment banking business," he added.
